Transparent Conductors Predictions¶

John El Berch

Model Fitting¶

Test all the models¶

This notebook uses the DataFit.py script, which contains a couple of auxiliary functions and an object class called DataFit, made to help streamline the whole process, while allowing to check the score using different categorical variables.

Important Notes¶

  • I will use the RMSLE as the score to tune the models' hyper parameters (since it is used in the Kaggle competition for the score as well). One note is that, in the Kaggle competition, they compute the RMSLE considering both outputs (the bandgap and the formation energy). Technically speaking, I am approaching this problem as tuning the hyperparameters considering both outputs separately, and then choosing the best model for each type of output.
  • The grids I defined contain a small number of parameters in order to save some computational time (considering I want to fit a large number of models with varying inputs)
  • I will create csv files that will contain the predicted values of Bandgap and Formation energy. These will be computed using the best identified models for each case, and the test.csv dataset. These predictions will be then submitted to Kaggle to check the performance
  • I won't taste the binary_number_of_atoms feature explored in the EDA, since it didn't showed any benefits

Preprocessing operations¶

I will add new features following the comments made in the corrections of the project. These have been defined below. Moreover, as a general preprocessing operation, the continous inputs will be standarized, and dummy variables extracted from the categorical variables of interest. PCA will be considered for one case. If PCA or polynomial features are included, the continous inputs will be standarized one final time before fitting the models.

df_test['spacegroup'] = df_test['spacegroup'].astype('category')

Define the new preprocessing features¶

New Variable 1: Deviations from ideal spacegroup data

In [ ]:
Spacegroup_df = pd.DataFrame({'alpha_theory' : [90, 90, 90, 90, 90, 90],
                             'gamma_theory' : [90, 90, 90, 120, 90, 120] , 
                            'spacegroup' : [206, 33, 227, 167, 12, 194]})
In [ ]:
prepro_df_train = pd.merge(left=Spacegroup_df,right=df_train.copy(), how='inner', on='spacegroup')
prepro_df_test = pd.merge(left=Spacegroup_df,right=df_test.copy(), how='inner', on='spacegroup')
In [ ]:
prepro_df_train['alpha_comparisson'] = prepro_df_train['lattice_angle_alpha_degree'] - prepro_df_train['alpha_theory']
prepro_df_train['gamma_comparisson'] = prepro_df_train['lattice_angle_gamma_degree'] - prepro_df_train['gamma_theory']
prepro_df_test['alpha_comparisson'] = prepro_df_test['lattice_angle_alpha_degree'] - prepro_df_test['alpha_theory']
prepro_df_test['gamma_comparisson'] = prepro_df_test['lattice_angle_gamma_degree'] - prepro_df_test['gamma_theory']

Create sigmoid feature

In [ ]:
def sigmoid(x):
    return np.exp(x) / (np.exp(x)+1) - 0.5
In [ ]:
prepro_df_train['alpha_sigmoid'] = sigmoid(prepro_df_train['alpha_comparisson'])
prepro_df_train['gamma_sigmoid'] = sigmoid(prepro_df_train['gamma_comparisson'])
prepro_df_test['alpha_sigmoid'] = sigmoid(prepro_df_test['alpha_comparisson'])
prepro_df_test['gamma_sigmoid'] = sigmoid(prepro_df_test['gamma_comparisson'])

Variable 2: Proportions between lattice constants

In [ ]:
prepro_df_train['a_to_b'] = prepro_df_train.lattice_vector_1_ang.to_numpy() / prepro_df_train.lattice_vector_2_ang.to_numpy()
prepro_df_test['a_to_b'] = prepro_df_test.lattice_vector_1_ang.to_numpy() / prepro_df_test.lattice_vector_2_ang.to_numpy()
In [ ]:
prepro_df_train['a_to_c'] = prepro_df_train.lattice_vector_1_ang.to_numpy() / prepro_df_train.lattice_vector_3_ang.to_numpy()
prepro_df_test['a_to_c'] = prepro_df_test.lattice_vector_1_ang.to_numpy() / prepro_df_test.lattice_vector_3_ang.to_numpy()

New Variable 3: Logit transformation of percentages

In [ ]:
'percent_atom_'

for element in ['al','ga','in']:
    for df in [prepro_df_test, prepro_df_train]:
        P = (df['percent_atom_'+element].to_numpy() - -0.01) / (1.02)
        OR = P / (1-P)
        df['logit_'+element] = np.log(OR)

New Variable 4: Log transformation of Bandgap energy

In [ ]:
prepro_df_train['log_bandgap'] = np.log(prepro_df_train.bandgap_energy_ev.to_numpy())

Fit the first series of models¶

  • Categorical to consider: spacegroup. number_of_total_atoms is considered a continous variable here.
  • Continous variables: Will include the new-generated variables
  • PCA? No

Define the helping lists of inputs, outputs and categorical variables¶

In [ ]:
output_list = ['formation_energy_ev_natom', 'log_bandgap']

categorical_list = ['spacegroup']

exclude_list = ['alpha_theory', 'gamma_theory', 'id', 'percent_atom_al', 'percent_atom_in', 'percent_atom_ga', 
                 'alpha_comparisson', 'gamma_comparisson', 'bandgap_energy_ev', 'number_of_total_atoms_cat', 'binary_number_of_total_atoms']

input_list = [var for var in prepro_df_train.columns.to_list() if var not in output_list+categorical_list+exclude_list]

Fit the third series of models¶

  • Categorical to consider: spacegroup. number_of_total_atoms is not considered at all.
  • Continous variables: Will include the new-generated variables
  • PCA? No

Define the helping lists of inputs, outputs and categorical variables¶

In [ ]:
output_list = ['formation_energy_ev_natom', 'log_bandgap']

categorical_list = ['spacegroup']

exclude_list = ['alpha_theory', 'gamma_theory', 'id', 'percent_atom_al', 'percent_atom_in', 'percent_atom_ga', 'number_of_total_atoms', 
                 'alpha_comparisson', 'gamma_comparisson', 'bandgap_energy_ev', 'number_of_total_atoms_cat', 'binary_number_of_total_atoms']

input_list = [var for var in prepro_df_train.columns.to_list() if var not in output_list+categorical_list+exclude_list]

Fit the log_formation energy¶

Initialize the DataFit object¶
In [ ]:
DF_3_1 = DataFit(prepro_df_train, continous_inputs=input_list, categorical_inputs=categorical_list, output=output_list[0], use_PCA = False)
Execute the FitAll() Method¶

This method will fit all the models, store the results as attributes

In [ ]:
DF_3_1.FitAll()

Final Takeaways¶

Which model was best?¶

In general, the second elastic net model (the one considering polynomial features), and the Gradient Boosted Regressors were the models that had the best overall scores for the training data using cross-validation. It is worth mentioning that, although surprising in appearance, the neural network model wasn't preferred in any case, despite the non-linear nature of the problem. This is in large ammount caused by the small number of hidden layers chosen and the small sampling space of the hyper-parameter tuning grid (due to computational cost).

Overall, and as it can be found in the Kaggle_Scores.csv file, the performance of all models was similar and overall poor. The best overall feature-set turned out to be the second, which involved using PCA.

To improve the performance of the models, some extra features to consider can include the distances between atoms, the angles between them, and other user element-dependent properties.

All in all, the project was a good experience to deepen the knowledge of different models, and the use of scikit learn.

What are the most important features according to the Random Forest model?¶

The most important features include the length of the third lattice vector, the lattice angle alpha and the concentration of element In. Some rankings included the concentration of Al, which was a variable I expected to have a large impact (based on the EDA). It surprised me to see many Random forests that didn't include this variable as one of the most importants. Additionally, the lattice angle beta was not included, which, again turned to be surprising since the EDA seemed to suggest otherwise.
